correctness.rationale: Every 13 successive odd integers lie in at most two consecutive blocks modulo 27. A fully specified 27-row triple table gives in one block each lower-digit-sum residue modulo 3, hence forces a zero total digit-sum residue for arbitrary upper digits. In any 39 odd numbers at difference 2 exactly 13 are multiples of 3, and dividing them by 3 yields 13 consecutive odd integers. One has ternary digit sum divisible by 3, so its original triple is not anti-Niven. Even integers cannot be ternary anti-Niven because base 3 is odd. The 38-term witness 86699+2j, 0<=j<38, has 38 explicitly recorded digit sums and gcd 1 each; the local script independently checks the 27 triples, all 243 arbitrary upper residue pairs, and the witness.

originality.rationale: The motivating primary study (arXiv:2308.05228v1) explicitly leaves upper bounds for bases of the form 2^r+1 unsettled while only proving lower bound b (Theorem 4.1); for b=3,d=2 its other stated upper bounds do not apply. A previous lower bound 7 for this exact pair also does not determine the maximum. Searches for 3-anti-Niven 2-AP sharp maxima, ternary coprime digit sums and 13-odd-number digit sums found no published equivalent or stronger covering result. Another primary article treats Niven (divisibility) rather than anti-Niven (coprimality). This is best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The 2023 primary paper explicitly left upper bounds in the b=2^r+1, d=2 regime open and gave only a lower bound. The exact maximum 38 at the smallest odd base b=3 closes the first natural case and identifies a structural obstruction using the base-27 digit-sum recurrence. The cutoff is mathematically motivated by the paper and is sharp with a concrete witness; it is not an arbitrary finite sample. It makes no claim about other bases or differences.
